title: Cap. X: Opponent parental-crime syllogism; immediate vs mediate; Pighius warn
pass_a_gloss: Opponent's major: children stripped of benefits their parents had taken for self and offspring because of some actual parental crime — those children pay the father's-crime penalties, and therefore the father's crime is imputed to them. Minor applied to Adam: every natural descendant, for that first polluting disobedience, loses the natural justice and uprightness Adam had received for himself and his line. Conclusion drawn: every natural descendant pays those paternal-crime penalties, so the crime is imputed. Placeus's fork if the conclusion is granted: take 'paternal crime' as the hereditary vice itself → then yes imputed, and immediately; take it as the cause of that vice (Adam's actual disobedience) → also imputed, but only through the inherent vice as means. Penalty timing: we pay nearby for the sin propagated into us, farther back for Adam's old act. Bare-immediate reading rejected: anyone who says we are born liable to Adam's trespass with no vice, fault, or depravity in us is repeating Pighius; Martyr explained and chiefly overthrew that error — reader, weigh whether those same blows hit Garissoles's thesis.
pass_b_english: Whoever, he says, are deprived of those benefits which those parents had received both for themselves and for their children because of some actual crime of the parents — those people suffer the penalties of the father's crime, and so the father's crime is imputed to them. But all Adam's posterity, because of that first disobedience of his by which he polluted himself, are deprived of those benefits which Adam had received for himself and for his posterity — namely, natural justice and uprightness. Therefore all Adam's natural posterity suffer the penalties of the father's crime, and so that paternal crime is imputed to them. What if I grant this conclusion? For paternal crime is understood either as the hereditary vice, or as the cause of that vice — Adam's actual disobedience. If the former, it is imputed, and indeed immediately. If the latter, that too is imputed, but by means of the inherent vice. We suffer the penalties proximately for our own sin propagated into us, and remotely for the sin once committed by Adam. But if someone says that we are all born liable to Adam's transgression immediately — that is, not because of any vice or fault or depravity that we have in ourselves — let him remember that this was Pighius's error as Peter Martyr explained it, and as it was chiefly confuted by these arguments. Consider them, reader, if you please, and whether they do not fight against D. Garissoles's sentence and arguments.
source_text: Qui, inquit, propter parentum crimen actuale aliquod, iis beneficiis privantur, quae parentes illi & pro se & pro liberis suis acceperant; illi paterni criminis poenas luunt, atque adeo paternum crimen illis imputatur. Atqui posteri omnes Adami propter primam illam ejus inobedientiam qua se polluit, privantur iis beneficiis, quae Adamus pro se & pro posteris suis acceperat, nimirum, justitia & rectitudine naturali. Ergo posteri omnes naturales Adami paterni criminis poenas luunt, adeoque paternum illis crimen imputatur. Quid si hanc conclusionem concedam? Paternum enim crimen vel vitium haereditarium intelligitur, vel causa illius vitii, actualis inobedientia Adami. Si prius, imputatur, & quidem immediate. Si posterius, imputatur id quoque, sed mediante inhaerente vitio. Luimus poenas proxime peccati nostri in nos propagati, remote vero peccati ab Adamo olim admissi. Quod si dicat aliquis, nos omnes transgressioni Adae nasci obnoxios, immediate, hoc est, non propter aliquod vitium, aut culpam, aut depravationem, quam in nobis habeamus, is meminerit sic fuisse Pighii errorem a Petro Martyre explicatum: atque his argumentis in primis confutatum: quae considera, Lector, si placet, annon pugnent cum D. G. sententia & argumentis.

lemmas.gloss: by means of the inherent vice

choices.decision: split hereditary vice (immediate) vs actual cause (mediate via inherent vice)
flag bare immediate liability without inherent vice as Pighius error per Martyr
